Classic New York-Style Bagels

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Makes 12 bagelsPrep 30 min active + 8-12 hours chillingCook 2-3 min boil + 18-20 min bake

Bagels are a beloved staple for breaking the Yom Kippur fast, offering a comforting and satisfying meal after a day of spiritual reflection and atonement. Traditionally served with cream cheese, lox, and an array of fresh toppings, they symbolize community and the return to nourishment, making the post-fast meal a cherished gathering.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (355 ml) warm water (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 teaspoons (7 g) instant yeast
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) barley malt syrup or granulated sugar
  • 4 cups (480 g) bread flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons (9 g) fine sea salt
  • For Boiling:
  • 8 cups (1.9 L) water
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) barley malt syrup or granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) baking soda
  • Optional Toppings:
  • Sesame seeds, poppy seeds, everything bagel seasoning

Method

  1. In a large bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer, combine the warm water, yeast, and 1 tablespoon of malt syrup (or sugar). Let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Add the bread flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or the dough hook of a stand mixer on low speed until a shaggy dough forms.
  3. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface or with the dough hook on medium speed for 8-10 minutes, until smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test (a small piece can be stretched thin enough to see light through without tearing).
  4. Lightly oil a clean bowl, place the dough in it, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, or until nearly doubled in size.
  5. Gently punch down the dough and divide it into 12 equal pieces (about 3 ounces or 85g each).
  6. Shape each piece into a tight ball. Then, using your thumb, poke a hole through the center of each ball. Gently stretch the hole to about 1 1/2-2 inches (4-5 cm) in diameter, creating the bagel shape.
  7. Place the shaped bagels on a lightly floured or parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving some space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight (8-12 hours). This slow, cold proof is crucial for developing flavor and chewiness.
  8. The next day, preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  9. In a large pot, combine 8 cups of water, 1 tablespoon of malt syrup (or sugar), and baking soda. Bring to a rolling boil.
  10. Carefully drop 2-3 bagels into the boiling water at a time, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Boil for 30 seconds to 1 minute per side. The longer they boil, the chewier the bagel will be.
  11. Using a slotted spoon, remove the boiled bagels, allowing excess water to drain. Place them on the prepared baking sheet. If using toppings, sprinkle them on the bagels immediately after boiling.
  12. Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until the bagels are golden brown and cooked through. Flip them halfway through baking for even browning.
  13. Transfer the baked bagels to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For the most authentic New York-style texture and flavor, do not skip the overnight cold proof in the refrigerator.
  • Barley malt syrup, available at specialty food stores or online, gives bagels their characteristic slightly sweet, malty flavor and glossy crust. Granulated sugar can be substituted, but the flavor will be slightly different.
  • Use bread flour, not all-purpose flour, as its higher protein content is essential for the chewy texture of a classic bagel.
